格.meaning: Beside a <part>tree</part>, <part>each</part> guest arrives in turn, and the tree sorts them onto its branches: kings at the very top, knights in the middle, the rest of us down on the roots. Where you sit shows your <kanji>status</kanji>.
格.on: Vultures in the tree know their status too: the top bird gets the best bit of the <sound>carc</sound>ass, the lowest gets the bones.

氏.meaning: A banner hangs from a hooked pole, drooping to one side, with a small knot dangling under its bar. It is stitched with a single word, the name every cousin, aunt and grandson shares: the <kanji>family name</kanji>.
氏.on: The family name is painted in gold right across a knight's <sound>shi</sound>eld.
氏.kun: '<sound>Oo</sound>!' gasp the cousins, as the banner rolls past on the back of a <sound>jee</sound>p.

民.meaning: Under the <part>clan</part> banner, a crowd gathers and opens one big <part>mouth</part>: farmers, bakers, children, all shouting together. No kings or lords here, just ordinary <kanji>people</kanji>.
民.on: The people chase a <sound>mean</sound> giant out of town for stealing all the bread.
民.kun: Then they share one enormous <sound>ta</sound>co with a hungry <sound>mee</sound>rkat.

紙.meaning: A <part>clan</part> of beavers chews <part>thread</part> and bark into mush, spreads it flat on a rock and leaves it in the sun. Next morning they peel off a thin white sheet you can write on: <kanji>paper</kanji>.
紙.on: A knight's <sound>shi</sound>eld turns out to be made of paper, and the first raindrop goes straight through it.
紙.kun: A <sound>ca</sound>rp folds the paper into a hat and plops it on a <sound>mee</sound>rkat's head.

温.meaning: You pour <part>water drops</part> into a <part>dish</part> and set it out under the <part>sun</part>. By lunchtime the water is just right for your toes: not cold, not hot, but nice and <kanji>warm</kanji>.
温.on: Too slow? Flip the heater's <sound>on</sound> switch, and the dish starts to steam.
温.kun: '<sound>Ah</sound>!' you sigh, toes in the warm dish, while a drummer beside you taps softly: '<sound>ta</sound>, <sound>ta</sound>.'

配.meaning: A <part>cobra</part> slithers from house to house with a crate of <part>dynamite</part>, leaving one stick on every doorstep. Nobody asked for one, but everybody gets one. That's how you <kanji>distribute</kanji> things.
配.on: Next it hands out jars of honey, one from every <sound>hi</sound>ve in the village.
配.kun: '<sound>Cu</sound>ckoo!' calls a clock, and a sheep bleats '<sound>Bah</sound>!' as each one gets its share.

重.meaning: A farmer tries to lift his whole <part>farm</part> onto his back, with a <part>thousand</part> sacks of potatoes piled on top. His knees wobble and his face goes red. It's far too <kanji>heavy</kanji>.
重.on: Right on top of the pile sits a single tiny <sound>jew</sound>el, and somehow that's the heaviest thing of all.
重.kun: '<sound>Oh</sound>!' groans the farmer, as a <sound>mo</sound>le pops up and adds one more potato.

誰.meaning: A <part>sparrow</part> lands on the podium in the middle of your <part>speech</part> and starts to chirp. Everyone stares at it, then at you. Is this your bird? The sparrow tilts its head and asks right back: <kanji>who</kanji> are you?
誰.on: Who left a <sound>swee</sound>t on the podium? The sparrow pecks the wrapper open.
誰.kun: Who threw these <sound>da</sound>rts? One just popped a <sound>re</sound>d balloon over the sparrow's head.
